$comment: DRAFT — NOT A REGISTRATION. Every field marked TO_BE_DECIDED is a product-owner decision (Daniel) and is deliberately left open here; a run against this file is not a registered run. When the numbers are set, this becomes registration_version 4 of code-awareness-roi.json (or its own registered file) and is frozen BEFORE the first arm runs. Drafted 2026-09-18 by Claude Opus 5 alongside #582 (find_affected_files).
registration_version: TO_BE_DECIDED (4 if it supersedes code-awareness-roi.json v3)
why_a_new_registration: v3 answered its question and the answer invalidated the comparison: `find_code` was offered in 44 of 44 runs and called in 0, so both arms ran the same grep behaviour and the measured difference (+0.8 Pp recall) is noise between two runs of one procedure. Two things were confounded — whether an agent REACHES for the graph, and whether the graph's answer HELPS. This design separates them.
question: (a) Adoption: offered a change-impact tool described graph-first, how often does an agent call it? (b) Effect: when the change-impact answer is in front of the agent, does it name more of the files the change really breaks, without naming more wrong ones?

A.name: grep
A.description: No MCP server at all — text search and file reads only. The control, identical to v3's control arm.

B.name: offered
B.description: `find_code` and `find_affected_files` offered over stdio MCP, nothing else changed. Whether the agent calls them is the observation, not a nuisance.

C.name: forced
C.description: Same tools, plus the `find_affected_files` answer for exactly the planned change already in the prompt. The agent cannot fail to use it.

arms.isolation: unchanged from v3: `--setting-sources project --strict-mcp-config --no-session-persistence`, fresh process per scenario and arm, cwd a throwaway worktree with no `.git`, graph moved out of the tree

adoption.definition: share of scenarios in which find_affected_files (and separately find_code) is called at least once; calls per scenario as a secondary figure
adoption.$comment: v3 measured 0 % for find_code. Any threshold here is a statement about the description and the name, not about the graph.

effect.from: arm C against arm A, paired per scenario
effect.context_increase_max_ratio: TO_BE_DECIDED (v3 allowed 1.25 x median on scenarios solved in both arms)

combined.$comment: Adoption and effect multiplied. Reported for completeness; reporting it AS the effect is what made v3 unreadable.

unit_and_truth.unit: one historical change to one file, at most one scenario per file
unit_and_truth.ground_truth: new type errors after applying exactly that file's diff, compared as (file, TS code, message) multisets, adjudicated by hand before any arm runs
unit_and_truth.$comment: The truth definition is not touched: changing the ruler and the tool in the same step would leave nothing comparable.

sample.$comment_fresh: MANDATORY. The 44 scenarios in ~/.bastra/eval/code-roi-v2/ were used to develop the symbol query this measures (offline tuning: entry specificity, the package-import narrowing threshold, the file-count cap). A number from them is a training number and must not appear as an effect estimate.
how_to_mine: CODE_ROI_OUT=~/.bastra/eval/code-roi-v4 node packages/eval/code-roi/v2/mine.mjs   — walks commits NEWEST first from a range end that must not overlap v3's range (v3's `range_end` is recorded in ~/.bastra/eval/code-roi-v2/scenarios.json); one scenario per file
CODE_ROI_OUT=~/.bastra/eval/code-roi-v4 node packages/eval/code-roi/v2/evidence.mjs   — builds the truth sets by typechecking before/after
CODE_ROI_OUT=~/.bastra/eval/code-roi-v4 node packages/eval/code-roi/v2/select.mjs   — applies the inclusion rules and freezes the scenario file with its seed
adjudicate the truth sets by hand and record a written reason for every removal
fill in the numbers above, freeze this file, THEN run run-arms-v3.mjs
sample.commit_range: TO_BE_DECIDED — must not overlap v3's range
sample.cost_note: v3 cost 13.15 $ for 2 arms x 44 scenarios. Three arms at the same size is roughly 1.5 x that; a smaller sample is a power decision, not a budget one.

statistics.method: paired bootstrap, 10 000 resamples, resampling scenarios with replacement

reporting_duties: Adoption from arm B, with its N, separately for each tool.
Effect from C vs A, paired mean with its 95 % interval, per-scenario rows.
Precision and context as in v3.
B vs A, labelled as adoption and effect combined, never as the effect.
That the offline figures on the v3 sample (recall 91.3 %, precision 52.4 %) are development data and carry no weight here.
An honest `underpowered` / `not_evaluable` where the sample does not support a verdict.
